newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq urges Britain to shift policy on Baghdad.
newsitem.headline: Iraq urges Britain to shift policy on Baghdad.

text.p: Iraq's ruling Baath party newspaper al-Thawra urged Britain's new government on Sunday to refrain from using human rights as a pretext to interfere in its domestic affairs.
"Britain is capable of easing or removing the hatred Iraqis and Arabs harbour towards it," the paper said in a front-page editorial.
It called on Prime Minister Tony Blair's Labour government to "relinguish employing the card of human and minority rights as a cover to meddle in the area's internal affairs."
It said Blair's government should rather focus attention on how to preserve human rights in Britain.
Thawra suggested the British government end its "silly" policy of defending Kurdish rights in Iraq and focus instead on what it called persecution of Kurds in Iran and Turkey.

It said Britian was to blame for the current situation in northern Iraq where rebel Kurds, under U.S. and British air protection, admininster their affairs outside the control of the central government in Baghdad.
"Last but not least, the new British government should be more realistic and view the issue of the (U.N.) embargo imposed on Iraq at least in the same way as other European (countries) do," it said.

The United States and Britain insist that United Nations sanctions imposed on Iraq for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait remain in force until Baghdad fully adheres to its obligations under the 1991 Gulf War ceasefire.
